terms.gloss: of (the owner, the whole, the amount, the quality)
terms.grammar: construction: the genitive case, with no preposition
terms.comment: Latin has no word for “of”; the genitive does its work: the owner (capillī capitis, the hairs of the head), the whole that a part is taken from (nēmō nostrum, none of us), an amount (aquae sextāriōs sex, six pints of water), and an age or a quality (annōrum novem, nine years old). Not with a name: “the city of Rome” is urbs Rōma, the two nouns in the same case.

terms.grammar: preposition with the ablative; ē only before consonants
evidence: Liv. 2.13.6: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus
Cic. Verr. 2.2.21: statua ex aere facta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: After a number or ūnus, and for the stuff a thing is made of.

terms.gloss: of, from (a part taken off a whole)
terms.comment: A piece taken from something, in plain and kitchen Latin: ungulam dē pernā, a hock off the ham.

terms.gloss: of (my father’s, of gold): an adjective instead of the genitive
terms.grammar: construction: an adjective agreeing with its noun
terms.comment: Latin likes an adjective for a family member or a material: domus paterna, the family house; pōculum aureum, a cup of gold.

phrases.latin: Vestrī autem capillī capitis omnēs numerātī sunt.
phrases.english: And the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

phrases.latin: nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē
phrases.english: none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day before

phrases.latin: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … frūstrāta custōdēs, dux agminis virginum inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit
phrases.english: Cloelia, a girl, one of the hostages, gave her guards the slip and swam the Tiber at the head of a band of girls, under the enemy’s spears

phrases.latin: sūme tibi ōllam, additō eō aquae sextāriōs sex et eō additō ungulam dē pernā
phrases.english: take a pot, put six pints of water in it, and put in a hock off the ham

phrases.latin: Hannibalem annōrum fermē novem, puerīliter blandientem patrī Hamilcarī ut dūcerētur in Hispāniam
phrases.english: Hannibal, about nine years old, coaxing his father Hamilcar like a little boy to take him to Spain

phrases.latin: vīvitur parvō bene, cui paternum splendet in mēnsā tenuī salīnum
phrases.english: he lives well on little whose father’s salt-cellar shines on a plain table

phrases.latin: utrum sit aureum pōculum an crustallinum an murreum an Tīburtīnus calix an manus concava, nihil rēfert
phrases.english: whether it is a cup of gold, of crystal or of agate, a mug from Tibur or a cupped hand, makes no difference
